test_title: PYST 73: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: During the electrolysis of brine, which of the following correctly matches the products formed at each electrode and in the solution?

options.text: Anode – Cl₂ , Cathode – H₂ , Solution – NaOH
Anode – H₂ , Cathode – Cl₂ , Solution – NaOH
Anode – NaOH, Cathode – Cl₂ , Solution – H₂
Anode – Cl₂ , Cathode – NaOH, Solution – H₂

solution:
The correct answer is __**Anode – Cl₂, Cathode – H₂, Solution – NaOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of electrolysis of an aqueous solution of **sodium chloride** (commonly known as **brine**) is industrially termed the **Chlor-alkali process**.
 
• When **electricity** is passed through brine, it decomposes to form **sodium hydroxide**, **chlorine**, and **hydrogen**. The name "Chlor-alkali" is derived from the products: "chlor" for **chlorine** and "alkali" for **sodium hydroxide**.
 
• At the **Anode** (the positive electrode), **chlorine gas (Cl₂)** is produced as chloride ions lose electrons (oxidation).
 
• At the **Cathode** (the negative electrode), **hydrogen gas (H₂)** is produced as hydrogen ions from the water gain electrons (reduction).
 
• The **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** solution is formed in the remaining liquid, typically near the **cathode** compartment.
 
• The overall chemical reaction representing this process is: **2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlorine (Cl₂)**: It is a versatile gas used primarily for **water treatment**, disinfecting **swimming pools**, and the manufacture of **PVC (Polyvinyl Chloride)**, disinfectants, **CFCs**, and pesticides.
 
• **Hydrogen (H₂)**: This byproduct is highly valuable as a **fuel**, for the hydrogenation of oils to produce **margarine**, and in the synthesis of **ammonia** for agricultural **fertilizers**.
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**: Commonly known as **caustic soda**, it is used for **de-greasing metals**, manufacturing **soaps and detergents**, in **paper making**, and for creating **artificial fibers** like rayon.
 
• **Brine**: It refers to a **saturated** or highly concentrated solution of **salt (NaCl)** in water. In a typical industrial setup, the concentration of salt is approximately **26%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the **electrolytic cell**, the migration of ions is specific: the negatively charged **chloride ions (Cl⁻)** migrate toward the **positive anode**, and the **hydrogen ions (H⁺)** (from water) migrate toward the **negative cathode**.
 
• The **membrane cell** and **diaphragm cell** are the modern technologies used to ensure that the **chlorine** gas produced does not react with the **sodium hydroxide**, as they would otherwise form sodium hypochlorite (bleach).
 
• The **Chlor-alkali industry** is one of the largest segments of the **chemical industry**, providing raw materials for thousands of downstream products including medicines and plastics.
